question.problem:
Find the general solution to the equation

$$
\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}-10\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+25y=8{e}^{5x}.
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, we need to find the complementary function ${y}_{c}(x),$ which is the solution to the homogeneous equation

$$
\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}-10\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+25y=0.
$$

Writing down and solving the auxiliary equation gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }^{2}-10\lambda +25 & =0 \\ (\lambda -5)^{2} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

So $\lambda =5$ is a repeated root, and therefore the complementary function ${y}_{c}(x)$ is

$$
{y}_{c}(x)=A{e}^{5x}+Bx{e}^{5x}.
$$

We now need to find the particular integral ${y}_{p}(x).$

The right-hand side of the inhomogeneous equation is $8{e}^{5x}.$ In this case, the constant factor in the exponent is $5$, which coincides with the double root of the auxiliary equation. Therefore, we assume a particular solution of the form

$$
{y}_{p}=\alpha {x}^{2}{e}^{5x},
$$

where $\alpha $ is a constant that is to be determined.

Calculating the first and second derivatives of ${y}_{p}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}{y}_{p}}{\text{d}x} & =\alpha (2x+5{x}^{2}){e}^{5x},\,\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}{y}_{p}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}=\alpha (2+20x+25{x}^{2}){e}^{5x}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute ${y}_{p},$ ${y}_{p}^{′},$ and ${y}_{p}^{″}$ into the ODE and solve for $\alpha :$

$$
\begin{aligned}\alpha (2+20x+25{x}^{2}){e}^{5x}-10\alpha (2x+5{x}^{2}){e}^{5x}+25\alpha {x}^{2}{e}^{5x} & =8{e}^{5x} \\ \alpha (2+20x+25{x}^{2}-20x-50{x}^{2}+25{x}^{2}){e}^{5x} & =8{e}^{5x} \\ 2\alpha {e}^{5x} & =8{e}^{5x} \\ 2\alpha  & =8 \\ \alpha  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
{y}_{p}(x)=4{x}^{2}{e}^{5x}.
$$

The general solution is given by

$$
y(x)={y}_{c}(x)+{y}_{p}(x),
$$

and therefore, the general solution in our case is

$$
y=A{e}^{5x}+Bx{e}^{5x}+4{x}^{2}{e}^{5x}.
$$
